title: The app slice of the agent runtime client: the two operations the legacy Java interface spans, the call type and the budget of a step, the login, the record write and its link, the guardrail check-code list and the route in front of the run read are not fixed by any source
source: Legacy RWB-TE-013 sections 3, 4, 7, 10, 11, 12 and 13; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.11; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2, T6.2 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 16, 41, 42 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 12; Ownership Map v1 (eight agent tables owner P10, eleven P10 operations, EV-08 owner P7); Template and Rules v1 §R3, §R4, §R5.5, §R6, §R7.3 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC8; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.8; 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: Six values the app slice needs are absent from the sources or disagree between them. (1) The legacy published interface AgentStepClient.runStep is a Java call, and the eleven P10 operations of TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 hold no run-submit operation and no link operation, so the two operations that carry the interface across the boundary have no method and no path in any source. (2) The call type is open: Arch v5 slide 16 shows the run as AgentRunWorkflow on the rwb-agent queue, Template and Rules DP-11 and DP-20 make the legacy in-process call a REST contract with a mock, and no source reconciles the two. (3) The budget disagrees: DP-11 fixes a 2 s client budget for a published interface, while agent_policy.timeout_seconds is 60 and NFR-010 allows the full 60 seconds before the rule result is used. (4) The per-service login of rwb-agent is required by DP-02, but the legacy section 3 names only the calling module identity SY-CASEWF, the agent identity SY-AGENT and the decision-log identity SY-DECLOG. (5) The decision record moves from the P7 DecisionLogWriter of one deployment to the local record of DP-03 and the EV-08 topic, and the link between the record and the run has no operation, so who writes the record, in whose transaction and how the link is stored are unstated. (6) The list of guardrail check codes, which carries the legacy value SCHEMA, is not a list of values in TSD P10 v2 T3.2, and the gateway-bff route in front of the run read has no name and no path. The story keeps the legacy behaviour and settles each value as an assumption.
evidence: Legacy RWB-TE-013 section 12 ('public interface AgentStepClient { AgentStepOutcome runStep(AgentStepRequest request) throws DecisionNotRecordedException; }' with the AgentStepRequest, RuleResult and AgentStepOutcome records and the decision log mapping), section 13 ('Adds column decision_log_id uuid to agent_run in migration V10_002__agent_run_decision_link.sql'), section 3 ('The calling module runs under its own service identity (for example SY-CASEWF)') and section 4 steps 2, 4 and 8; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.1 (eleven operations, none a step submit or a link), T3.2 (LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-AGENT-RUN, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS and the other lists, no guardrail check-code list) and T6.2 ('service identities for jobs and agents'); FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.11 (fall back to the rule result when an agent is unavailable, integration points Workbench and Model gateway); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 ('TMP AgentRunWorkflow: 60 s, then rule result') and slide 41 (schema rwb_agent, own login, base /api/recovery/<name>/v1); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-03, DP-11, DP-19 and DP-20, §R6 (RWB-TE-007 retired, dependencies point to RWB-PLT-E1071-CON) and NFR-010
area: Agent client: operations, call type, budget, identity, decision record and route
owner_role: Solution architect with the P10 service owner and the owners of rwb-decision, rwb-case and rwb-access
proposed: Fix the step operation as POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-steps and the link operation as PUT /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId}/decision-record, with the legacy request and answer members unchanged in name and meaning; treat the step operation as the single recorded exception to the 2 s budget with the policy timeout of 60 seconds as its budget, and leave the real cross-service hop to RWB-ITG-TE013-ITG; keep the legacy record mapping and let the calling step write the record through the local library in its own transaction, with the link stored by the link operation on agent_run.decision_log_id; name the login 'the rwb-agent login (DP-02)' until the platform agrees the string; keep the check code as a value of the guardrail result of RWB-P10-E1058-APP; reach the run read through the gateway-bff route. Every value is settled in the assumption rows cited and no literal is invented.

title: The client contract: the operation paths and the member types beyond the legacy Java records, the refusal set, the 409 of an in-flight repeat, the record reference and the route in front of the run read are not specified by any source
source: Legacy RWB-TE-013 sections 7, 12 and 13; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.11; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 16, 41, 42 and 43; Ownership Map v1 (eleven P10 operations, EV-08 owner P7, decision_log_entry owner P7); Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.5, §R7.2 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC6; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.3; 12.8; 19 Out of scope
description: Five elements of the contract are open in the sources. (1) No source names the method and the path of a step submit or of a link, although TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 fixes eleven other P10 operations. (2) The member types beyond the legacy Java types are given only as names: the JSON shape of RuleResult.result, the map of inputs, the decimal scale of confidence and the price fields, and the detail text of each refusal are unstated. (3) The refusal set is not fixed for these operations: the legacy interface throws one exception (DecisionNotRecordedException with MSG-P7-003) and the platform uses 401, 403, 409, 422 and 503, but no source says which of them a step submit answers in which condition, and the legacy repeat rule (R-UNI-40, the repeat returns the first outcome) says nothing about a repeat that arrives while the first run is still in flight. (4) The record reference the outcome carries and the link stores is a UUID of the record library, whose shape and read-back belong to rwb-decision and are not written in any source for this key. (5) The gateway-bff route in front of the run read has no name and no path, and the run read itself is the baseline's, so this document can only restate the members this key reads.
evidence: Legacy RWB-TE-013 section 12 (the records, the decision log mapping and 'Idempotency: stepKey, used as the agent run idempotency key and as the decision log lookup key for repeats') and section 7 (AC6 raises DecisionNotRecordedException with MSG-P7-003; AC7 returns the first outcome on a repeat); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.1 (API-P10-001 to API-P10-011 with their error sets, none a step submit or a link) and T3.1 (DF-AGT-058 decision_log_id CROSS_REF uuid); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (rwb-agent IN: REST GET /agent-runs/{id}, GET/POST /agent-policies (admin); TMP AgentRunWorkflow) and slide 42 row 08 (DecisionRecorded produced by all 19 on rwb.decision-record.v1); Ownership Map v1 (GET /admin/agent-runs owner P10; decision_log_entry owner P7); Template and Rules v1 §R4 (base and naming) and §R5.5 DP-03, DP-11, DP-13, DP-19 and DP-20
area: Contract: operation shapes, refusal set, record reference and route
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-agent with the solution architect and the owners of rwb-decision and rwb-case
proposed: Declare the two operations under the base /api/recovery/agent/v1 with the legacy member names in their JSON spelling and their types fixed by this document, the refusal set 401, 403, 409, 422 and 503 with 409 for a step key whose first run is still RUNNING and for a run that already holds another record, the record reference as the library's UUID with the read-back of rwb-decision, and the route as a pass-through of one hop whose name is agreed with the route contract. The app, deployment and calling stories build against these shapes and the three fakes.

title: The deployment slice of the agent runtime client: the chart values, the login secret, the topic rights of the shared decision-record topic, the worker concurrency, the alert thresholds, the route path and the capacity figures are not specified by any source
source: Legacy RWB-TE-013 sections 3, 13 and 14; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.11; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T6.2 and T7 (NFR-010); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 16, 20, 41, 42 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11 and 12; Ownership Map v1 (outbox, inbox and idempotency tables owner PLT); Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.5, §R6 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC6; 10 Authority; 11 Data; 12.3; 12.5; 13 Solution plan; 19 Out of scope
description: Six environment values of this key are absent from every source. (1) The per-service login of rwb-agent has no name, no secret name and no grant list beyond 'schema rwb_agent only'. (2) The release takes only the publish right on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1, and no source states the partitions, the replication factor, the retention, the retry topic name or the .dlt topic name of that shared family, nor whether the service or the platform owns the producer credential the library uses. (3) The Temporal worker concurrency, poller count, activity timeouts and the worker identity of rwb-agent are not given. (4) The 60 second policy budget and the 10 percent fallback target are targets (NFR-010, FSD P10 v3 A2.11) with no measurement point, no percentile and no alarm threshold. (5) The pod capacity, the KEDA minimum and maximum, the backlog trigger and the operator alarms have no figures. (6) The gateway-bff route path and the runbook wording are unstated. No source names a Quartz job table for this key either: RWB-TE-007 is retired and its dependence points to RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, so no job table and no job admin read is deployed.
evidence: TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T6.2 ('service identities for jobs and agents') and T7 (NFR-010 'An agent returns an answer within its target, after which the rule result is used and the case still routes | Under 60 seconds'); FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.11.1 (agent fallback rate below 10 percent per month); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (topics with a .dlt route), slide 16 (queue rwb-agent, topic rwb.decision-record.v1 as a shared topic of all 19 producers), slide 41 (one login per service, base /api/recovery/<name>/v1) and slide 44 (no shared Quartz tables; a Schedule or an event-started workflow in the owning service); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 11 (namespace rwb-recovery, one task queue per service, KEDA scales workers on backlog); Template and Rules v1 §R4 and §R6 (RWB-TE-007 retired) and §R5.5 DP-02, DP-03, DP-09, DP-10 and DP-19
area: Deployment: identity and secrets, topic rights, worker, gates, route and capacity
owner_role: SCB IT infrastructure and the DevOps team with the ACE platform team and security
proposed: Deploy the api and worker from the template with the login through a secret reference and grants on rwb_agent only, the migration job of V10_002__agent_run_decision_link.sql, the worker registration on queue rwb-agent with KEDA on backlog, the publish right on rwb.decision-record.v1 with the platform retry and .dlt bindings, the six dashboard panels and five alert rules with their thresholds as reviewed environment values, the route publication and six runbook entries, and record every environment value as a reviewed value per environment rather than a template constant. No table, no topic and no business value is created.

title: Case intake agent live at L1 in rwb-agent: the service login, the decision code, the business date of the stale check, the item key set, the invalid-verdict refusal, the migration order and the segment rule are not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-028 sections 3, 4, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12 and 13; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.7, A2.6.3.1 and A2.6.3.2; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.0, T3.1, T3.2, T-A.1 and T-A.2 API-P10-010 and API-P10-011; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 14, 16, 20, 42 and 43; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11, 12 and 13; Recovery Workbench Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.4, §R5.5 DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-13, DP-15 and DP-19 and §R9; Ownership Map v1 (tables agent_run, agent_policy, agent_prompt, agent_feedback and decision_record under P10; api rows GET /cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs and POST /agent-runs/{runId}/feedback under P10)
section: 3. Preconditions; 5. Exception paths; 7. Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC9; 8. Business rules BR1 and BR3; 10. Authority; 12.1; 12.3; 13. Solution plan
description: The app slice needs seven values that no source fixes, and none of them is invented. (1) The per-service login of rwb-agent is required by DP-02, and the legacy section 10 names only the agent identity SY-AGENT and the roles. (2) The decision code D6 is the assumed code of LOV-DECISION in the legacy BR3, and the local decision record of a feedback has no field list of its own once DP-03 moves the write to the service. (3) The business date against which agent_run.data_as_of is compared for the stale warning of AC9 has no owner operation in this key, because the freshness rule of the FSD names v_ace_batch_status, which belongs to rwb-source-data and is not a dependency of this service. (4) The item key set of an intake output is not listed; the legacy story fixes the item SUMMARY only. (5) The status and the message of a verdict outside LOV-FEEDBACK are not stated: the legacy operation gives 422 for a missing reason with MSG-P7-005 only. (6) The place of V10_008__agent_feedback.sql in the service's Flyway ordering is not fixed, because no source lists the P10 migration sequence. (7) The rule that settles two approved policy rows in force for one segment is not stated, although the FSD allows a row with an empty product group. The story keeps every legacy value - the policy version P2, the mode L1, the prompt PR3, the decision code D6, the item SUMMARY, the 1,000 characters of the reason and the nine acceptance criteria - and settles each open value as an assumption.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-028 sections 3 (the approved policy P2 with mode L1 from 2027-01-25), 4 (the orchestrator run and the decision log write), 7 AC1 to AC9 (every legacy value and message), 8 BR1 ('only runs in mode L1 for the case segment are returned'), BR3 ('decision D6 (LOV-DECISION, assumed code)') and BR5 ('one feedback per run and item; the intake summary is item SUMMARY'), 10 (roles only, no login name), 12 (the two operations on the monolith base, AgentOutput and AgentFeedbackRequest, the decision log mapping and the errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503) and 13 (migration V10_008__agent_feedback.sql and the components); FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.7.3.1 VR-P10-007-1 (v_ace_batch_status), A2.6.3.1 VR-P10-006-1 (MSG-GEN-001) and A2.6.3.2 (the policy fields and the empty product group); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.0 (the version column), T3.1 (DF-AGT-008, DF-AGT-009, DF-AGT-010, DF-AGT-036 to DF-AGT-060, DF-AGT-097 to DF-AGT-102), T3.2 (LOV-AGENT, LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-FEEDBACK, LOV-DECISION, LOV-PRODUCT) and T-A.2 API-P10-010 and API-P10-011; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 (P10 calls P7 for events and P1 by REST, not by a case read), slide 14 (P7 owns the central decision ledger), slide 16 (P10 in and out, queue rwb-agent, topic rwb.agent.events.v1), slide 20 (gateway-bff and the outbox of every service), slide 42 (A2 row 08, DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1) and slide 43 (A3 row 28, AgentRunCompleted); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11, 12 ('Agent run with rule fallback' in the kit) and 13 (a child workflow per stage, the case router); Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.4, §R5.5 and §R9; Ownership Map v1 tables and api rows under P10 and P7
area: Agent runtime: identity, decision record, stale check, item keys, verdict refusal, migration order and segment rule
owner_role: Solution architect with the P10 service owner and the owners of rwb-case and rwb-decision
proposed: Name the service identity 'the agent service identity (DP-02)' until the platform fixes the login, with grants on rwb_agent only. Write the D6 record through the local decision-record library with the legacy mapping and publish DecisionRecorded as rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on rwb.decision-record.v1, keyed by the case ID. Compare agent_run.data_as_of with the data date of the case record read and show no banner when the case record returns none. Keep the item key SUMMARY as the only item of the intake output. Refuse a verdict outside LOV-FEEDBACK with 422 and the platform message MSG-GEN-001. Keep the legacy file name V10_008__agent_feedback.sql and let the sequence order decide its place. Settle two policy rows in force for one segment in favour of the row that sets both segment fields, with an empty product group meaning every product group. Each value is carried by an assumption row of this key and is confirmed at the wave 2 contract freeze with the owners of rwb-case, rwb-decision and the platform libraries.

title: Case intake agent at L1 contract in rwb-agent: the member types of the answer and of the request, the record event type name, the route path, the 409 rule and the invalid-verdict refusal are not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-028 sections 7, 11 and 12; Recovery Workbench Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.4, §R5.5 DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-13, DP-15 and DP-19 and §R9; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2, T-A.1 and T-A.2 API-P10-010 and API-P10-011; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.6.3.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 20, 41, 42 and 43; Ownership Map v1
section: 3. Preconditions; 7. Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC6; 10. Authority; 11. Data; 12.1; 12.3; 15. Screens and states
description: The contract slice needs five values that no source fixes. (1) The legacy story names the members of AgentOutput and of AgentFeedbackRequest and three lengths, and the TSD gives the table columns, but no source gives the REST member types, the maximum lengths of summary, gapType and reason beyond the three lengths of the table, or the form of the feedback member inside the answer. (2) DP-03 names the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 and not the event type, and two contract documents of this run write the type name differently, so the name used on the topic is a settled value. (3) The path and the name of the gateway-bff route in front of the two operations are not specified, although DP-19 requires the route. (4) The legacy operation carries both the If-Match header and the one-feedback-per-run-and-item rule and gives one message for both, and no source states which check answers the 409 first. (5) The status and the message of a verdict outside LOV-FEEDBACK are not stated. The contract keeps the legacy members and values and settles each open value as an assumption, and it declares no monolith path and no table of another service.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-028 section 7 (the nine criteria and their values), section 11 (DF-AGT-036 to DF-AGT-060 and DF-AGT-097 to DF-AGT-102) and section 12 ('GET /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs', 'POST /api/recovery/v1/agent-runs/{runId}/feedback', AgentOutput with runId, agent, agentVersion, mode, status, summary, gaps, confidence, dataAsOf and feedback, AgentFeedbackRequest with itemKey, verdict and reason at most 1,000 characters, the If-Match header, the errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 and the one-feedback-per-run-and-item rule); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (agent_feedback, item_key varchar(20), verdict varchar(10), reason varchar(1000)) and T-A.2 API-P10-010 and API-P10-011; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.6.3.1 VR-P10-006-1 (MSG-GEN-001); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 16 (P10 topic and queue), slide 20 (gateway-bff, one hop, 2 s), slide 41 (P10 first API path and topic), slide 42 (A2 row 08) and slide 43 (A3 row 28); Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.4, §R5.5 and §R9; Ownership Map v1 api rows under P10 and the table agent_feedback under P10
area: Contract: answer and request member types, record event type, route path, conflict rule and invalid-verdict refusal
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-agent with the solution architect and the owners of rwb-decision and rwb-case
proposed: Fix the two operations on the base /api/recovery/agent/v1 with the legacy members and the legacy refusals; fix the member names of the answer and of the request and leave the physical types to the review with their owners; declare the record event as rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on rwb.decision-record.v1 with the retry and .dlt topics, keyed by the case ID; publish the two operations behind one gateway-bff pass-through route of one hop and 2 s and take its path from the edge contract; settle the 409 by the unique key first and the If-Match version second, both carrying MSG-GEN-004; refuse a verdict outside LOV-FEEDBACK with 422 and MSG-GEN-001. Each open value is carried by an assumption row of this key and is confirmed at the contract freeze with the owners of rwb-decision, rwb-case and the edge.

title: Case intake agent at L1 deployment in rwb-agent: the login, the migration order, the topic partitions and retry names, the alert window and thresholds, the worker and probe values and the route path are not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-028 sections 3, 4, 5 and 13; Recovery Workbench Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.5 DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19 and §R9; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 16, 20, 41, 42 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 11; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T7; Ownership Map v1

source: Legacy RWB-E2-029 sections 3, 4, 7, 11, 12, 13 and 14; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.8 and FEAT-AGT-08; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2, T5.2, T-A.1 API-P10-006 to API-P10-011 and T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 16, 41, 42 and 43; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 13 (DeviationWorkflow on rwb-deviation); Ownership Map v1 (eight agent tables owner P10, eleven P10 operations, deviation owner S8, interaction owner P1, decision_log_entry owner P7, parameter and reference tables owner P3); Template and Rules v1 §R3, §R4, §R5.5, §R5.7, §R7.3 and §R9

title: The contract slice of the deviation screening evaluation and L1 on one segment: the S8 raise path and members, the parameter keys, the member types of a consumed answer, the sealed decision-entry read, the service login and the route path are not specified by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E2-029 sections 3, 11, 12, 13 and 14; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.8; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.2 (LOV-DEVIATION is named by the legacy story only), T-A.1 API-P10-010 and API-P10-011 and T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 16, 41, 42 and 43; Ownership Map v1 (deviation owner S8, interaction owner P1, decision_log_entry owner P7, parameter and reference tables owner P3); Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.5 and §R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC6; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.7; 12.8; 19 Out of scope
description: Five elements of the contract are open in the sources. (1) The raise of a deviation is an in-process interface in the legacy story with six request members and two answer members, and no source gives its REST method, its path, its answer resource or its refusal codes, so the contract declares the members and marks the path as not specified. title: The contract baseline of the legal document agent: the OCR-text and checklist operations and member names, the legal-action read, the run-start path, the route, the paging and member types, and the event family beyond EV-28 are not specified by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E2-030 sections 11, 12, 14 and 17; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.9; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2, T3.3 and T-A.1 to T-A.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 41, 42 and 43; Ownership Map v1 (eleven P10 operations, six agent tables of this key, AgentRunCompleted owner P10); RWB P5 E2025 CON sections 7, 11 and 12.2; Template and Rules v1 R3, R5.5 and R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC6; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.3; 12.8
description: Five elements of the contract are open in the sources. (1) The OCR-text read of a document and the checklist read of a case type have no operation path and no member names, although the legacy document read, getFields and getChecklist become owner contracts. (2) The legal-action read of rwb-litigation for a case has no path in any source and no S4 contract story sits in the C row of this key. (5) EV-28 AgentRunCompleted is the only agent event any source names; the family pattern admits an event for the completion of an evaluation or for an item status and no source names one, so the contract declares EV-28 only and publishes no pack content. title: The app slice of the agent monitoring dashboard v2: the drift step's place, the segment on the run row, the decision-log filter and elements, the notice operation, the policy values, the migration number, the range limits, the login, the route path and the name of the right are not fixed by any source
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-031 sections 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12, 13 and 15; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.6 (FEAT-AGT-06); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2, T6.1 and T-A.1 to T-A.2 (API-P10-009); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13 to 20 and 41 to 44; Ownership Map v1 (eight P10 tables, eleven P10 operations, EV-28, AgentRunWorkflow); Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.5, §R7.3 and §R9; the published contracts of RWB-P10-E1063-CON and RWB-P7-E2005-CON
section: 3. Preconditions; 5. Exception paths; 7. Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC7; 9. State transitions; 10. Authority; 11. Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.5; 12.6; 13. Solution plan; 15. Screens and states
description: Nine values the app slice needs are absent from the sources or disagree between them, and none may be invented. (1) The drift check: the legacy story puts the step agentDrift after agentRunDaily inside JOB-15 at 01:30, no source names a Schedule for it in the target, and JOB-15 is the reporting extract of rwb-reporting in the job map, so the place of the step in the target is a decision. (2) The segment: the legacy story reads recovery_case.product_group and recovery_case.region_code, the target carries the same facts on the run row as DF-AGT-059 and DF-AGT-060, and no source states that this story reads them only and never the case table. (3) The override figures: the legacy P7 query interface DecisionLogQuery.byAgentVersion(agentVersion, from, to) becomes the rwb-decision contract of RWB-P7-E2005-CON, which declares the query parameters caseId, caseIds, decision, ruleId, ruleVersion, approver, from, to, page and size and the answer elements of the audit read, and declares no filter on the agent version and none of recommendation, final_call and override_reason that the override rate and the override reasons need. (4) The notice: no source names the operation of the rwb-comms notification path. (5) The policy values: the legacy story assumes drift_points 10 and a minimum of 20 feedback entries per week and segment, adds no window length, and no source states the key, the shape or the loading of agent_policy.watch_measures beyond the field DF-AGT-019. (6) The migration: only V10_001 of the service is named by a source, and the legacy migration V10_007 adds two segment columns that TSD P10 v2 T3.1 already declares, so the number, the content and the index names of the migration are open. (7) The limits: MSG-GEN-002 names 1 and 92 days and no source names the parameter key that holds them. (8) The login: DP-02 requires one login per service and no source names it. (9) The route: the gateway-bff route in front of SCR-46 and the read has no name and no path. One conflict is recorded here: the read is authorised under Platform administration R in the legacy story section 12 and TSD P10 v2 T6.1, and under Rules and parameters R in TSD P10 v2 T-A.1 API-P10-009.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-031 section 3 ('RWB-E1-063 is done: agent_run_daily is written by JOB-15', 'RWB-E2-005 is done: the P7 decision log query interface', 'each L1 policy holds watch_measures with drift_points 10 (assumed) and minimum feedback 20 per week per segment (assumed)'), section 4 step 5 ('JOB-15 Reporting extract: after the daily rows, runs the drift check'), section 12 ('GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-metrics', 'Job: JOB-15 ... this story adds step agentDrift after agentRunDaily', 'Interface called: P7 DecisionLogQuery.byAgentVersion(agentVersion, from, to)'), section 13 ('migration V10_007__agent_run_segment.sql adds segment_product_group varchar(15) and segment_region_code varchar(10) to agent_run'), section 14 (MSG-GEN-002 'naming 1 and 92 days'); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (DF-AGT-059, DF-AGT-060, DF-AGT-019), T6.1 (Platform administration R), T-A.1 API-P10-009 (Rules and parameters R) and T-A.2 API-P10-009; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 (JOB-15 Reporting extract, owner rwb-reporting) and slide 16 (P10 contracts); RWB-P7-E2005-CON section 12.1 and its data table (the ten query parameters and the eleven audit elements); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-02, DP-03, DP-07, DP-10 and DP-13.
proposed: Put the drift step in the workflow of the v1 Schedule rather than in a new one; read the segment from the run row; read the override figures through the rwb-decision contract with the agent-version filter and the three elements added as an additive change; name the notice path by its owner; hold the policy values in watch_measures; name the migration V10_007 with the legacy index and one index on agent_feedback; hold the two range limits as configuration; name the login 'the rwb-agent login (DP-02)'; register the screen route under RWB-PLT-N001-CON; and take the right of API-P10-009 as the declaring source while recording the legacy name.

title: The contract slice of the agent monitoring dashboard v2: the member types of the v2 element, the paging, the names of the drift inputs, the agent-version filter, the notice operation and the route path are not fixed by any source
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-031 sections 7, 11 and 12; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.6; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1, T3.2 and T-A.2 API-P10-009; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41 to 44; the published contracts of RWB-P10-E1063-CON and RWB-P7-E2005-CON; Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.5 and §R9
section: 3. Preconditions; 5. Exception paths; 7. Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC6; 10. Authority; 11. Data; 12.1; 12.2; 12.5; 12.6; 12.8; 13. Solution plan
description: Six elements of the v2 contract are open in the sources. (1) The element types: TSD P10 v2 T-A.2 gives only the names of AgentMetric[] and no type or length for members beyond four decimals, and the legacy section 12 gives one flat list of names with no type at all. (2) The paging: the legacy section 12 declares no page size and the v1 contract fixed the paging of the same read, so v2 must not respecify it and cannot derive it. (3) The names of the drift inputs and of the verdict members of the element are not fixed by any source, although DF-AGT-019 declares watch_measures as jsonb and DF-AGT-100 declares the verdict list. (4) The agent-version filter of the decision-log read and the three elements the override figures need are not declared by RWB-P7-E2005-CON, so the consumed side of the contract cannot be completed from a source. (5) The operation of the rwb-comms notification path is named by no source. (6) The gateway-bff route in front of the read and the override panel has no name and no path. The contract fixes the member names and leaves the types to the review with their owners, which is the only position the sources support.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-031 section 12 ('Response: 200, array of AgentMetric (agent, policyVersion, promptVersion, modelVersion, segment, mode, date, runs, fallbackRate, acceptanceRate, correctionRate, overrideRate, feedbackCount, latencyP50Ms, latencyP95Ms, tokens, costThb, reconciled)'), section 11 (the DF ids of decision_log_entry and agent_alert); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T-A.2 API-P10-009 ('Response AgentMetric[]', 'Request Query: agent, segment, version, from, to'), T3.1 (DF-AGT-019 watch_measures jsonb, DF-AGT-100 verdict LOV-FEEDBACK) and T3.2 (LOV-AGENT-ALERT COST_CAP and DRIFT); RWB-P7-E2005-CON section 12.1 and its data table; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (naming notes) and slide 43 (EV-28); Template and Rules v1 §R4.
proposed: Fix the seven added member names, their four-decimal rule and the additive rule of major version 1; keep the paging and the held-date status of RWB-P10-E1063-CON unchanged; name the drift inputs after the watch_measures members; declare the agent-version filter and the three elements of the decision record as an additive change of the rwb-decision contract; name the notice path by its owner; and register the route under RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

title: The deployment slice of the agent monitoring dashboard v2: the topology, alert thresholds, login, route path, the Schedule update path and the consumer group ownership are not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-E2-031 sections 3, 4, 5, 12 and 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 20, 37, 41 and 44; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T6.2 and T7; the published contracts of RWB-P10-E2031-CON; Template and Rules v1 §R4, §R5.5 and §R9
section: 3. Preconditions; 5. Exception paths; 7. Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC6; 10. Authority; 11. Data; 12.2; 12.6; 13. Solution plan; 19. Out of scope
description: Six deployment values of this key are absent from every source. (1) The login: DP-02 requires one login per service and no source names the rwb-agent login, the ACE database administrator's grants or the secret entry. (2) The route: the gateway-bff route in front of the v2 read and the override panel has no name and no path, and the edge story owns the specification. (3) The alert thresholds: no source gives a threshold, a window or a percentile for the sent-empty, short-week, unreconciled-month or step-not-run alerts, and no measurement point is named for the 2 s client budget. (4) The topology: cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, probe timings, the host, the SKU and the budget are absent. (5) The Schedule update path: the v1 release registered AgentRunDailyRollup and no source states how the added step is re-registered without creating a second Schedule or a second run. (6) The consumer group: the group of rwb.agent.events.v1 belongs to rwb-reporting and no source states what the agent release verifies about it. Retention and partition values of the topic are likewise unstated and are not invented here.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-031 section 12 (the job and its idempotency key), section 13 (the feature flag rwb.agent.monitor-v2 and the migration); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 ('schema rwb_<name> with its own login; REST under /api/recovery/<name>/v1 behind gateway-bff; Kafka topic rwb.<name>.events.v1; Temporal task queue rwb-<name> in namespace rwb-recovery') and slide 44 (Schedule with overlap policy SKIP and catch-up window); TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T6.2 (service identities) and T7 (NFR-008, NFR-010); Template and Rules v1 §R4 and §R5.5 DP-02, DP-03, DP-10 and DP-19.
proposed: Reference the login through a secret reference and name it 'the rwb-agent login (DP-02)'; register the route under RWB-PLT-N001-CON and leave its path to the edge story; expose every threshold and topology value as a chart value with a name and the rule that it is not hard-coded; update the Schedule in place and verify the two steps on one workflow identity; and verify the consume right of rwb-reporting without creating its consumer group.
